verdict.rationale: Azure's own documentation describes fine-grained RBAC scoping and managed identities that let applications obtain Microsoft Entra tokens without handling credentials. Together these give a narrowly scoped, credential-less identity that could be handed to an agent. The evidence does not show agent-specific patterns, short-lived or temporary credential issuance, or guarantees that the identity cannot escalate its own permissions. Missing for 10: documented agent-specific credential patterns, explicit temporary/time-bound credential issuance, escalation-prevention controls, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native team, agents get their own leash — documented patterns for handing an agent temporary, narrowly-scoped credentials it cannot escalate

citations.quote: Azure RBAC is an authorization system built on Azure Resource Manager that provides fine-grained access management to Azure resources.
Allow one user to manage virtual machines in a subscription and another user to manage virtual networks
Applications can use managed identities to obtain Microsoft Entra tokens without having to manage any credentials.
